newsitem.title: USA: PECO says Pa. Limerick 2 nuke back on line.
newsitem.headline: PECO says Pa. Limerick 2 nuke back on line.

text.p: PECO Energy Co said Thursday the 1,055 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at its Limerick nuclear complex synchronized to the power grid earlier today.
"It went back on line at 3:45 (0345 EST)," a company spokesman said, adding it could resume full output as early as Friday.
During restart from an outage that began December 18, the unit was manually shut Wednesday when a vibration problem was discovered at a recirculation pump in the turbine.
Limerick 2 was taken off line a little more than a week ago to repair a leaking seal in its condenser.
The nearby 1,055 MW Limerick unit 1 was producing at 100 percent capacity.
Both Pottsdam, Pennsylvania, units are wholly-owned and operated by PECO Energy.
